items.title: Sportiello interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2020
items.q: I was reading George Shearing’s biography you know, during the war in England.

ctx.x: I think that we were lucky that a hundred years went by and didn’t have such a big pandemic going on. Because I think the last event that this, even that can be considered similar to this was the Spanish flu, even though back then I think the numbers of people that died was unbelievable. Like more than the fatalities of the two wars I’ve heard. But you know there is something to be said — I saw an interview of an Italian ex-elementary school teacher that she is still alive, I think one hundred and some years old,…

go dancing normally during the weekends, and then the alarm would go off and they would try to hide in the basements. But then when the alarm would stop they would go up again to the club and keep dancing. You know? And the same thing, I was reading George Shearing’s biography you know, during the war in England. Guys — they were going out and play gigs every night. And then the planes would come, the Germans, and drop a few bombs, and of course some people died. But it didn’t stop them from running their regular…
Do you think it’s partly because we are bombarded with so much information 24 hours a day that it stifles us?
